trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up, left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,5). So the line goes up.
The line must go right: left is number 10, which comes later; around the edge to (5,4) is number 6, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (5,5), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out down or around the edge to (2,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going around the edge to (4,1) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (down from number 3) was wrong, so the line must go around the edge to (2,1).
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5). So my guess (right from number 4) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes around the edge to (3,5).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going around the edge to (4,1) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
The line must go right: left is number 9, which comes later.
Cell (4,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going around the edge to (1,2) would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes right.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
